title: Air India Launches 'Easy Connect' From Amritsar, Linking Punjab to 27 Global Destinations
excerpt: Punjab travelers can now fly internationally through Delhi without changing terminals or rechecking baggage, as Air India expands its hub-and-spoke model to its second regional city after Varanasi.
body:
• Air India has launched two daily 'Easy Connect' flights from Amritsar, connecting Punjab travelers to 27 international destinations through Delhi without terminal changes or baggage rechecking.
  • Passengers can complete immigration procedures at Amritsar before departure, simplifying international travel from the regional city to destinations across North America, Europe, the UK, Australia, and Southeast Asia.
  • Amritsar is the second city after Varanasi to join the program, with Ahmedabad, Goa, and Kochi planned next as part of India's broader ambition to develop 44 airports in a hub-and-spoke network.
  • Air India also plans to introduce inbound Easy Connect flights to Amritsar within two months, allowing international arrivals to complete immigration at their final destination rather than at the first port of entry.

How Easy Connect Works

Air India's Easy Connect program eliminates the traditional pain points of connecting through a major hub. Passengers departing from Amritsar can complete through check-in, drop baggage, and clear immigration at their home airport. Their checked luggage transfers automatically to the final international destination — no need to collect and recheck it at Delhi.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=KFV-XAkD12Q

The airline operates two daily feeder flights from Amritsar to Delhi, timed to align with its international departure schedule. The morning service connects to European destinations including London Heathrow, Paris, Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Zurich, and Rome. The evening service feeds into North American routes to New York, Newark, San Francisco, Chicago, Toronto, and Vancouver, as well as Melbourne and Sydney in Australia.

All 27 international destinations are reachable within four hours of arriving at Delhi, according to the airline.

Part of a National Aviation Strategy

The Amritsar launch is the second under India's hub-and-spoke aviation model, following Varanasi's introduction in June. Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha announced plans at the Amritsar launch event to develop four hub airports and 40 spoke airports — a total network of 44 airports providing seamless international connectivity.

Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu described the hub-and-spoke approach as an "aviation sovereignty" model for India. The government aims to develop 100 airports and 200 heliports over the next decade, reducing India's dependence on foreign transit hubs like Dubai, Singapore, and Bangkok for connecting international passengers.

Delhi currently serves as the only hub airport. Ahmedabad is expected to become the next spoke airport, with Goa and Kochi also in the pipeline. Air India plans to eventually extend the network to hubs in Mumbai and Bengaluru as well.

Why This Matters for Punjab's Diaspora

The service is particularly significant for Punjab, home to one of India's largest overseas communities. Families, students, business travelers, and overseas workers from the region frequently travel to Canada, the United States, the UK, and Australia — all now accessible through a single coordinated itinerary from Amritsar.

Previously, most international passengers from Punjab had to travel to Delhi independently before beginning their long-haul journey, adding complexity, cost, and time. The Easy Connect model brings international transit procedures to the regional level, making Amritsar a genuine starting point for global travel rather than just a domestic airport.

"The inbound 'Easy Connect' model is expected to be introduced from Amritsar within the next two months."

— Air India statement

Inbound Flights Coming Soon

Air India has also announced plans to introduce inbound Easy Connect flights to Amritsar within the next two months. Under the current system, international passengers arriving in India must complete immigration and collect baggage at their first port of entry — typically Delhi — before taking a domestic flight to their final destination.

The inbound Easy Connect model will allow passengers to complete immigration and collect baggage at Amritsar itself, making it a true seamless connection in both directions. Air India said it would be the first Indian carrier to implement the Standard Operating Procedure for inbound hub-and-spoke operations.

Before You Book

Passengers using Easy Connect flights from Amritsar should note that Indian nationals traveling internationally through the service must complete DigiYatra enrollment before departure. Web check-in and Customs declaration facilities are not currently available at spoke airports under the Easy Connect process.

Tickets are available through Air India's website, mobile app, contact center, and travel agents. Travelers should confirm connecting international flight timing from Delhi and carry valid passports and travel documents.
nri_angle: Punjab's large overseas community — with frequent travel to Canada, the US, UK, and Australia — gains a direct international gateway at Amritsar with seamless baggage and immigration handling.
